SUPPRESSED IS TERMINAL. promote() matches tier = 'cold' and nothing else, so a suppressed edge is not merely refused, it is not addressed. unsuppress() returns an edge to COLD, never straight to hot. A duplicate insert reports the existing edge's TIER, so reflection is told when it has rediscovered something the Commander rejected.

ALL CREATES LAND HOT. There is no tier parameter on addNode/observe/infer: a colder partition is only ever reached by a move, which is what makes 'demotion and partitioning are the same mechanism' true of the API and not just the schema.

Origin check verified by me line by line, not taken on report. AttachmentSource uses whole-origin equality via SylKit's WebOrigin — the same type already guarding the admin WebView's bearer token, so there is one rule with one implementation rather than two that can drift. WebOrigin normalises scheme (http/https only), host via url.host(percentEncoded:false) which is the PARSED AUTHORITY and therefore defeats https://paired.host@evil.com, and effective port so :443 and omitted compare equal. Structural equality on three fields; no string matching anywhere. Refused in tests: prefix (.ts.net.evil.com), suffix (admin.<host>), userinfo, port mismatch, scheme downgrade to http (these fetches carry a live bearer token), javascript/data/file/about/custom schemes, and ids ../../logs and syl:attachment:../../logs rejected BEFORE the id can become a path segment. AttachmentSource.init is failable with no fallback, so 'allow everything' is unrepresentable. url(for:) puts its own composed output back through verify(), so the guard sits on the only path to a URL rather than beside it. Loader tests assert the fetcher call count is 0 — the guard stops a request rather than returning a Result nobody reads.

LocalStore.goals(limit:), goal(id:) and todos(goalId:). goals() orders by 'targetDate IS NULL, targetDate, title COLLATE NOCASE' — the NULL term because SQLite sorts NULLs first and a goal with no date is not more urgent than one due this month, the same reasoning the server's todos_agenda_idx states. Nothing is filtered out: abandoned and dormant are real outcomes with their history intact, and a read that hid either would be the accumulated-guilt design proposal B refuses. todos(goalId:) required a new indexed todo.goalId column, denormalised out of the payload and backfilled by SylDatabase.backfillTodoGoalLinks so an upgraded device does not report that nothing has ever happened on every goal; it returns closed to-dos too, because most evidence is finished work.

completeTodo(id:idempotencyKey:now:), completeReminder(...), snoozeReminder(id:minutes:idempotencyKey:now:) and createTodo(text:idempotencyKey:now:id:) in LocalStore, each a single database.queue.write containing both halves and a shared private enqueueIntent that makes a repeated key a no-op rather than a rollback. The flush was not touched. Atomicity is proved rather than assumed: a test installs a BEFORE INSERT ON outbox trigger that aborts, and asserts the to-do is still open afterwards — verified by mutation, since splitting the write into two statements makes exactly that test fail. createTodo also needed todo.pendingKey, because the contract gives a to-do no clientId and there is otherwise nothing tying the optimistic row to the server's copy; SyncEngine.synchronise settles it after a pull has actually landed.

snoozeReminder takes minutes and has no parameter that could carry an instant, so 'the server owns the new time' is structural rather than a rule to remember — SnoozeReminderRequest.until exists and this path cannot reach it. nextFireAt is left exactly as the server last stated it, in the payload AND in the indexed column the day sorts on. The ask is stored as reminder.deferralRequestedAt: the instant he asked, never a fire time. Two tests guard it — one asserts the payload is a duration with until nil, the other reads the raw row and asserts no stored instant is later than the moment he asked. Verified by mutation: adding nextFireAt = now + minutes to that UPDATE fails the second test, and revealed that the first assertion had been reading the payload model and could not see a column write, which is now asserted separately.

Driven through the real outbox, not by asserting a key is non-nil. At the store: a double tap on a completion, a deferral and a capture each leave exactly one outbox row and one local change. Through SyncEngine with a real Outbox and a recording gateway: a completion is pushed once and the second synchronise has nothing to send; a completion that fails carries the identical key on the retry; a capture pushed and pulled back leaves one to-do rather than two, and is kept rather than retired when the pull never landed. That last pair is the case a key alone cannot cover — a to-do has no clientId, so applying once is a property of the sweep and the pull together, not of the key.

A refusal queues nothing. Extended once beyond the brief: completing a capture the server has never heard of is also refused, because its only id is one this device minted, POST /todos/{id}/complete against it can only be NOT_FOUND, and the sweep would then replace the row with the server's still-open copy — the completion would undo itself with nothing said. Guarded twice, on purpose. Both places, one write path. TodoOrdering.swift — pure, stable, 21 tests. Deadline, then pinned, then recency; reads no stored priority, asserted by reflecting over Todo rather than by comment. The precedence was genuinely disputed (device SQL and the server index both led with pinned DESC) and the epic lead settled it deadline-first: a pinned undated to-do above one due in two hours is the list lying about what is urgent. Undated sorts LAST — SQLite's NULLs-first default was a live bug. The last term is recency, not staleness, and capture is why: a to-do he just wrote down sorting to the bottom of 500 undated rows would look like a capture that did nothing. Agreement with openTodos is asserted against a real database because that read takes a LIMIT: a disagreement hands the function the wrong 100 of 500 and it arranges the wrong 100 immaculately.

GoalRisk.swift: silence (now minus last activity > cadence, strictly greater — the seventh day of a seven-day cadence is when it is due, not when it is late; measured from createdAt when nothing has ever been linked) and arithmetic (required rate vs observed rate). Every degenerate case degrades to nothing: no cadence, cadence <= 0, no target date, target in the past, target today, no target value, goal younger than 7 days, and a metricKey this device cannot measure. GoalHorizon.swift: month <= 45 days, season <= 150, year <= 400, life beyond — derived from the span between createdAt and targetDate and never stored.
